scope: Only the new strict Bazel Windows XML error wrapper reader, its synthetic controls and main-call wiring; read the retained raw-log validator and cleanup for context.
conclusion: No confirmed new false-positive acceptance found in this narrow static scope.
findings: The XML reader first reruns the unchanged raw-log validator requiring exactly the original two failed cases, 0 passed, 0 ignored, 31 filtered and two distinct bounded positive descendant PIDs at the original survival assertions.

It requires one testsuites root with exactly one testsuite child, exact suite name and counters tests=1/failures=0/errors=1, exactly one running testcase and one error with the literal exit code 101. Extra failure, skipped, testcase or wrapper children are rejected.

The sole system-out must match the actual validated raw log after only UTF-8 BOM decoding, CRLF normalization and edge whitespace normalization. XML counters alone cannot turn a different raw test outcome into a rejection demonstration.

Main still requires Bazel exit 3, exact fresh log/XML report selection, and the original source restoration plus Git-clean finalizer. No native test selector, timeout or production source was changed by this XML adaptation.
The new controls define two accepted encodings and eighteen rejected synthetic structures/log mismatches. They are separate synthetic reader controls, not native evidence.
boundaries: This reviewer did not run the controls, download the original ZIP or execute any native test.
The peer's reported original Bazel Windows wrapper shape and its prior source-bound replay are not independently re-proven by this static review.
